title: Parkland housing proposal deferred
subtitle: Also heritage property standards, light trespass rules, a lobbyist registry, lease renewals and election donor privacy.
overview: The committee spent most of the afternoon on a staff report about building affordable housing on city land. It recommended receiving the report {{vote:m7}}. It then recommended deferring any action on Hugh Guthrie Park and Sleeman Park until Council has received the Housing Affordability Strategy {{vote:m10}}. An amendment that would have swapped in city parking lots and limited the housing to government-owned or co-operative housing was defeated {{vote:m9}}. No parkland will move toward development for now.

The committee also recommended a heritage minimum standards amendment to the property standards by-law {{vote:m2}}. It recommended three not-for-profit lease renewals {{vote:m3}}. It recommended that staff draft a by-law regulating light that spills from one property onto another {{vote:m6}}. It recommended a lobbyist registry by-law and code of conduct, with a registrar appointment {{vote:m11}}. It also asked the Province to change how donor addresses are shown in municipal election filings {{vote:m12}}.
After a closed session on a land matter, the Mayor reported only that information was received and staff were given direction. These are recommendations to Council, which will consider them later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a by-law amendment setting minimum maintenance standards for designated heritage properties, going to Council on July 23 and taking effect July 31 if adopted {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended 10-year leases for the Guelph Youth Music Centre and the Navy League, Guelph Branch, and a 20-year lease for the Royal City Tennis Club {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended that staff draft a by-law or property standards amendment regulating light trespassing between private properties, plus guidelines encouraging full cut-off fixtures {{vote:m6}}.
The committee received the report on strategic real estate partnerships on underutilized city-owned assets {{vote:m7}}.

The committee recommended deferring any action on the report, including studies and a request for expressions of interest at Hugh Guthrie and Sleeman Parks, until Council receives the Housing Affordability Strategy {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended approving the Lobbyist Registry By-law and Code of Conduct, appointing Suzanne Craig as Lobbyist Registrar and authorizing a contract for those services {{vote:m11}}.

The committee recommended asking the Province to stop publishing donor and candidate street addresses online, with addresses of donors over $100 kept on separate forms viewable only in person {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On parkland housing, staff said the two parks were chosen because they could be developed quickly with existing servicing. Staff said they were "torn" because the city already needs more parkland. Several councillors said they could not support using parks, and some wanted the city land inventory and the Housing Affordability Strategy first.

Delegates for co-operative housing and a housing charity supported using public land and argued affordability should be permanent, not limited to a set term. Water-protection and neighbourhood delegates opposed giving up parks, citing tree canopy, groundwater recharge, the city's water supply limits and a landfill beneath one site.

Councillors questioned whether a land shortage is the real barrier, citing staff figures on short- and long-term supply. Supporters said public land lowers costs and unlocks federal funding. Some councillors wanted any request for expressions of interest to prioritize county social housing and protect affordability against resale.

On light pollution, a delegate described a neighbour's floodlights shining into homes. Staff said the by-law would cover only light trespassing onto another property, enforced on complaint, with education rather than enforcement for general light pollution. Holiday lighting and city safety lighting would not be targeted.

On heritage standards, delegates and councillors raised the gap for listed but undesignated buildings and called for a vacant building registry. Staff said extending the by-law to all listed properties would add many more owners and would need further consultation.
